She said she and her family reflected on the period of his passing and are grateful to all who stood by them. She said their prayers, kind words, presence, calls, messages, thoughtful gifts, and generous contributions towards his funeral meant more to them.
Joke appreciated them for honouring his life, celebrating his legacy, and standing by them as they said their final farewell to a beloved husband, father, grandfather, colleague and friend.
The 40 days have come and gone, and as we reflect on this period, my family and I want to express our deepest and most heartfelt gratitude to you all for standing by us after the passing of my beloved husband, Pa Olu Jacobs.
“Your prayers, kind words, presence, calls, messages, thoughtful gifts, and generous contributions towards his funeral have meant more to us than words can adequately express. Every gesture of love, kindness and support brought us comfort and reminded us that we were surrounded by people who genuinely cared.
“Thank you for honouring his life, celebrating his legacy, and standing with our family as we said our final farewell to a beloved husband, father, grandfather, colleague and friend.
“We do not take your love and generosity for granted. We are truly humbled and deeply grateful.
May God bless you and your families abundantly, replenish what you have given, and continue to strengthen us all. With heartfelt appreciation and love.”
LEADERSHIP reported that the late veteran’s son, Olusoji, announced his demise, saying he died on the 16th of September, 2026.
On Wednesday evening, September 29th, a Night of Tributes/Service of Songs was held for the veteran at Glover Memorial Hall, 19 Marina Road, Lagos Island.
As expected, many Nollywood stars graced the occasion to pay their last respects to the Nollywood legend. The likes of Richard Mofe-Damijo, Funke Akindele, Sola Sobowale, Shaffy Bello, Juliet Ibrahim, Desmond Elliot, Jide Kosoko, Adebayo Salami, Femi Adebayo, Kate Henshaw, IK Ogbonna, Emeka Ike, and more were in attendance.
A day later, he was laid to rest in the presence of his family.
Present at the occasion were the First Lady of Lagos State, Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu; Lagos State Deputy Governor Dr Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat; Abike Dabiri; and former Ogun State Governor Senator Ibikunle Amosun.
